unit.title: Using devices: finding help and fixing common problems

objectives.text: Access and navigate structured help tools to identify and attempt appropriate solutions to common technical issues.

lesson.title: Finding Help and Fixing Common Problems
lesson.summary: Use official help tools to identify a sensible first step for common device, connection, login or app problems, and know when to ask for support.

objectives.text: Access and navigate structured help tools to identify and attempt appropriate solutions to common technical issues.

sections.heading: Start with a structured help source
sections.body: When an app or device is not working, use a structured help source such as an in-app help menu, official support centre, FAQ or trusted workplace guide. Describe the problem clearly when searching, including any error message but never a password or verification code. Step-by-step guidance can help you identify a safe first action rather than guessing.

sections.heading: Try straightforward checks
sections.body: Common first checks include confirming a connection, closing and reopening an app, checking whether an update is available, or using the official password-reset process. Read the guidance fully before acting and check that it matches your device. Do not disable security features or install unknown software just to make a problem disappear. Keep a note of what you tried.

sections.heading: Know when to stop and ask
sections.body: If a problem continues, involves sensitive information, or asks you to take an unfamiliar security action, stop and seek appropriate support. Use an official contact route, workplace IT support or a trusted person. Explain what happened, what the device showed and which safe steps you tried. This gives support staff useful information without sharing credentials or private codes.

practice.prompt: A fictional email app closes whenever it opens. Which is the best first source of guidance?
options: The app's official help menu or support centre
A link in an unexpected pop-up
A request to share the account password
An unknown file offered in a chat
practice.explanation: An official help menu or support centre is a structured source for identifying a safe response to an app problem.

practice.prompt: A fictional device cannot connect to a familiar wi-fi network. Which is a sensible straightforward check?
options: Check the device's connectivity settings and the official help guidance.
Turn off all account security settings.
Give a verification code to a stranger.
Install software from an unknown advert.
practice.explanation: Checking connectivity settings and official guidance addresses the stated problem without bypassing security.

practice.prompt: A support page asks a learner to reveal a password before it can help with a problem. What should the learner do?
options: Stop and use an official support route instead.
Post the password in a public forum.
practice.explanation: A legitimate support process should not require a learner to disclose a password, so they should stop and use an official route.
